results.prompt: Which model performed best and why?
results.text:
### Best model and why
- **XGBoost** has the lowest error on both tests: hold-out WAPE 1.57% (MAPE 1.58%) vs Naïve 2.59%, and 3-month rolling backtest WAPE 2.14% vs Naïve 2.28% (54 forecasts).
- It tracks the level (bias 0.49%) and most of the seasonal swing, using lag, rolling-mean and month features with shallow, regularised trees.
- Caution: at the 3-month horizon its margin over Naïve is small (2.14% vs 2.28%).

Sources: reference notebook (notebook run 2026-11-12 (FRED data to 2026-09)).

results.prompt: Explain MAPE vs WAPE using our results.
results.text:
### MAPE vs WAPE with our results
- **MAPE** averages each month's percentage error, so every month counts equally.
- **WAPE** divides the total absolute error by total demand, so big months count more. It tracks the real cost of mis-planned volume.
- Part 1 Naïve (Feb–Dec): MAPE 17.35% but WAPE 15.84%: the small spring and winter months had the largest percentage misses. Working: WAPE = 270 / 1705.
- Part 2 Naïve (hold-out): MAPE 2.64%, WAPE 2.59%: close, because the index moves in a narrow band.

Sources: reference notebook (notebook run 2026-11-12 (FRED data to 2026-09)).

results.prompt: Did the product show seasonality or a trend?
results.text:
### Seasonality and trend
- **Seasonality is real but moderate** (STL seasonal strength 0.59; trend strength 0.93). Peak months: Jul 1.028, Sep 1.026, Jun 1.021; weakest: Dec 0.978, Jan 0.973.
- In the test year the actual seasonal swing was 9.6% with the peak in Jul. SARIMA (shape correlation 0.70) and Holt-Winters (0.66) followed the shape best; Naïve is flat by construction.
- Part 1 has only 12 simulated months: one cycle, so seasonality cannot be separated from trend there.

Sources: reference notebook (notebook run 2026-11-12 (FRED data to 2026-09)).

results.prompt: Why did the Random Forest look good in-sample but fail in Part 1?
results.text:
### Why the Random Forest looked good in-sample but failed (Part 1, simulated demand)
- Scored on its own training months (Mar–Dec 2023) it reached MAPE 8.51%: that is fit, not forecasting.
- On unseen months (walk-forward Jul–Dec 2023) it was worst: MAPE 31.38%, WAPE 25.23%, vs Naïve 18.05% / 15.96%.
- Trees cannot predict below the range they were trained on, and with 4–9 training rows they kept forecasting summer levels while demand fell.
- The weather-adjusted regression was best: MAPE 12.00%, WAPE 11.98%.

Sources: reference notebook (Part 1, simulated demand).

results.prompt: What production and distribution plan do you recommend?
results.text:
### Production and distribution (suggestions)
- Oct 2026: plan around 95.30 with a working range of 91.14–96.61 (SARIMA 80%); keep upside capacity to 98.05 (95% high).
- Nov 2026: plan around 94.93 with a working range of 88.37–95.38 (SARIMA 80%); keep upside capacity to 97.23 (95% high).
- Dec 2026: plan around 93.53 with a working range of 86.64–94.45 (SARIMA 80%); keep upside capacity to 96.52 (95% high).
- Wind production down gradually into winter, and re-plan monthly as each new FRED release arrives.
- These are recommendations from a category proxy, not orders.

Sources: reference notebook (notebook run 2026-11-12 (FRED data to 2026-09)).
